what_its_for: This eye drop is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial eye infections, including bacterial conjunctivitis (also called 'pink eye'). It kills the bacteria causing your eye infection and helps clear up redness, discharge, and irritation in your eye.
how_to_take: 1. Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water before using the drops. 2. Tilt your head back and look up at the ceiling. 3. Gently pull down your lower eyelid to create a small pocket. 4. Hold the dropper tip directly over your eye and squeeze one drop into the pocket of your lower eyelid. Do NOT let the dropper tip touch your eye, eyelid, fingers, or any surface, as this can contaminate the drops. 5. Gently close your eye for 1 to 2 minutes. 6. Press your finger gently on the inner corner of your eye (near your nose) for about 1 minute. This helps prevent the medicine from draining into your throat. 7. If you need drops in both eyes, repeat these steps for your other eye. 8. Replace the cap on the bottle tightly after each use.
dosing: For adults and children 1 year of age and older: Days 1 and 2 (first two days): Place 1 drop in the affected eye(s) every 2 hours while you are awake, up to 8 times per day. Days 3 through 7: Place 1 drop in the affected eye(s) up to 4 times per day while you are awake. Always follow the specific instructions given by your doctor or pharmacist, as your dose may be different.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular dosing schedule. Do NOT use a double dose to make up for a missed one. Try to use your drops at the same times each day to help you remember.
storage: Store the bottle at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Do NOT freeze this medication. Keep it away from heat and direct light. Keep this and all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the drops after the expiration date printed on the bottle. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: 1. Do NOT wear contact lenses while you have a bacterial eye infection. Talk to your doctor before restarting contact lens use. If your doctor does allow contact lens use during treatment, remove your contacts before putting in the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in. 2. Do NOT touch the dropper tip to your eye, skin, fingers, or any surface to avoid contaminating the solution. 3. Avoid rubbing your eyes. 4. Do NOT share this medication with anyone else, even if they have the same symptoms. 5. Avoid driving or operating machinery right after using the drops if your vision is temporarily blurry.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: severe eye pain, swelling, or increased redness that gets worse instead of better; vision changes or loss of vision; signs of a serious allergic reaction such as severe rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing, or dizziness; eye discharge that is getting worse; symptoms that do not improve after a few days of treatment; accidental swallowing of the eye drops. Also call your doctor if you develop a skin rash anywhere on your body, as this could be a sign of an allergic reaction.
when_it_works: You may begin to notice improvement in your symptoms such as less redness, discharge, and irritation within 1 to 2 days of starting the drops. However, it is very important to finish the full course of treatment even if you feel better early. Stopping too soon can allow the bacteria to come back and make the infection harder to treat. Most people complete a full 7-day course of treatment.
special_populations: Children: This medication is approved for use in children 1 year of age and older. It should not be used in infants under 1 year old unless specifically directed by a doctor. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Because only a very small amount of the eye drop enters the bloodstream, the risk to the baby is considered low, but always discuss this with your healthcare provider before using. Elderly patients: No special dose adjustments are typically needed for older adults, but always follow your doctor's instructions. Patients with allergy to fluoroquinolone antibiotics (such as ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, or moxifloxacin): Tell your doctor before using this medication, as you may be at higher risk for an allergic reaction.
